events.title: Emperor Decius orders all Romans to sacrifice to the gods
events.description: Decius required every inhabitant of the empire to sacrifice before officials and obtain a certificate proving it. Christians who refused faced death, in the first empire-wide persecution of the Church.
events.html: Decius required every inhabitant of the empire to sacrifice before officials and obtain a certificate proving it. Christians who refused faced death, in the first empire-wide persecution of the Church.

events.title: Pope Leo X excommunicates Martin Luther
events.description: The bull Decet Romanum Pontificem formally cut Martin Luther off from the Catholic Church after he refused to recant. The break hardened the divide that became the Protestant Reformation.
events.html: The bull Decet Romanum Pontificem formally cut Martin Luther off from the Catholic Church after he refused to recant. The break hardened the divide that became the Protestant Reformation.

events.title: Washington defeats the British at the Battle of Princeton
events.description: After a night march from Trenton, Washington's army routed a British force at Princeton, New Jersey. Coming days after Trenton, the victory revived the American cause and pushed the British out of most of New Jersey.
events.html: After a night march from Trenton, Washington's army routed a British force at Princeton, New Jersey. Coming days after Trenton, the victory revived the American cause and pushed the British out of most of New Jersey.

events.title: Britain reasserts control over the Falkland Islands
events.description: HMS Clio under Captain James Onslow arrived at the Falklands and required the small Argentine garrison at Port Louis to leave. Argentina has disputed British sovereignty over the islands ever since.
events.html: HMS Clio under Captain James Onslow arrived at the Falklands and required the small Argentine garrison at Port Louis to leave. Argentina has disputed British sovereignty over the islands ever since.

events.title: Joseph Jenkins Roberts becomes Liberia's first president
events.description: Joseph Jenkins Roberts, born free in Virginia, was inaugurated as president of the newly independent Republic of Liberia. Liberia became the first independent republic in Africa.
events.html: Joseph Jenkins Roberts, born free in Virginia, was inaugurated as president of the newly independent Republic of Liberia. Liberia became the first independent republic in Africa.

events.title: Meiji Restoration returns power to Japan's emperor
events.description: Forces from Satsuma and Choshu seized the imperial palace in Kyoto and an imperial decree abolished the Tokugawa shogunate. The young Emperor Meiji's government launched Japan's rapid modernisation.
events.html: Forces from Satsuma and Choshu seized the imperial palace in Kyoto and an imperial decree abolished the Tokugawa shogunate. The young Emperor Meiji's government launched Japan's rapid modernisation.

events.title: Construction of the Brooklyn Bridge begins
events.description: Work started on John Roebling's suspension bridge across New York's East River. Completed in 1883 under his son Washington and daughter-in-law Emily, it was then the longest suspension bridge in the world.
events.html: Work started on John Roebling's suspension bridge across New York's East River. Completed in 1883 under his son Washington and daughter-in-law Emily, it was then the longest suspension bridge in the world.

events.title: Mussolini's speech to parliament opens his dictatorship
events.description: In a speech to the Italian Chamber of Deputies, Mussolini declared he alone took responsibility for all that had happened, including the murder of Giacomo Matteotti. The speech launched his open dictatorship.
events.html: In a speech to the Italian Chamber of Deputies, Mussolini declared he alone took responsibility for all that had happened, including the murder of Giacomo Matteotti. The speech launched his open dictatorship.

events.title: US Congress proceedings are televised for the first time
events.description: The opening session of the 80th Congress was broadcast on television, a first for the American legislature. Regular television coverage of both chambers followed only decades later.
events.html: The opening session of the 80th Congress was broadcast on television, a first for the American legislature. Regular television coverage of both chambers followed only decades later.

events.title: Alaska becomes the 49th US state
events.description: President Eisenhower signed the proclamation admitting Alaska to the Union. Purchased from Russia in 1867, it became the largest state by area, more than twice the size of Texas.
events.html: President Eisenhower signed the proclamation admitting Alaska to the Union. Purchased from Russia in 1867, it became the largest state by area, more than twice the size of Texas.

events.title: Bush and Yeltsin sign the START II arms treaty
events.description: In Moscow, George H. W. Bush and Boris Yeltsin agreed to cut their strategic nuclear arsenals by about two-thirds and ban multiple-warhead land-based missiles. The treaty never fully entered into force.
events.html: In Moscow, George H. W. Bush and Boris Yeltsin agreed to cut their strategic nuclear arsenals by about two-thirds and ban multiple-warhead land-based missiles. The treaty never fully entered into force.

events.title: NASA's Spirit rover lands in Mars's Gusev Crater
events.description: Cushioned by airbags, Spirit bounced to a halt on Mars on the evening of 3 January, US time. Planned to last 90 days, it explored for over six years and found evidence of past water.
events.html: Cushioned by airbags, Spirit bounced to a halt on Mars on the evening of 3 January, US time. Planned to last 90 days, it explored for over six years and found evidence of past water.
